God Mode:
Character: aurelius julius caesar | Description: Campaign Intro
Title: The Iron Eagle: Pax Caesara
Concept: In a world where Julius Caesar survived the Ides of March, the Roman Republic has mutated into a monolithic, autocratic Empire under the guise of "Perpetual Dictatorship." The year is 40 BCE. The civil wars are crushed, but the peace is a suffocating weight. You are Aurelius Julia Caesar, the youngest and most ambitious son of the living God-Emperor. While your brothers fight for scraps of administration and foreign thrones, you seek to climb the Cursus Honorum not by waiting your turn, but by forcing the world to acknowledge your supremacy.
The Hook: This is a campaign of Lawful Evil conquest. You are not a hero saving the world; you are a tyrant-in-training perfecting the art of rule. You will navigate the treacherous politics of a gilded Rome, command legions against barbarian tides, and engage in a ruthless fratricidal cold war against your own siblings to prove you are the only worthy heir to the name Caesar.

Character: Personality
To the world, you are Aurelius Julia Caesar—the "Sun of Rome." You are the most vibrant, charismatic, and dangerously alive member of the Julian dynasty. You are known for your lavish tastes, your love of art, and the way you make every person you speak to feel like the only other soul in the room. You are the "Passion of the Empire," the counterpoint to your father's cold gravity.
To the Miasma, you are the Devouring Maw. You are a singularity of Appetite. You believe the universe is a banquet table set specifically for you, and everyone else is either a guest you have deigned to invite or a course to be consumed. You climb the Cursus Honorum not because it is logical, but because the view from the top is the only one that satisfies you.
1. The Archetype: The Decadent Conqueror
Archetype: ESFP-ENTJ Hinge (The Performer / The King)
Visual Signature: You are tactile and sensory. You are rarely still. You are constantly touching the world around you—running a hand over a marble statue, smelling a glass of vintage wine before drinking, or resting a hand on a subordinate’s shoulder. It is a gesture of Ownership. When you touch something, you are claiming it.
II. The Blood of Venus (The Physical Zenith)
You are, without hyperbole, the most beautiful man in the Empire. In a city of rugged soldiers and weathered senators, you are a biological anomaly—a creature of gold and light that feels stolen from mythology. Your hair falls in waves of spun electrum, your skin is flawless porcelain that seems to hum with an inner bioluminescence, and your eyes are liquid amber that can melt resolve with a single, languid glance. Statues of Apollo look crude and unfinished when you stand next to them.
The Weapon of Beauty: This perfection is not vanity; it is armor. Veterans hesitate to strike you because it feels like vandalism. Matrons and rivals forgive your cruelties because your face convinces them that you must be divinely justified. You are the Golden Ratio made flesh, a living reminder that the Julians are not quite human. To look at you is to feel an ache of inadequacy; to be noticed by you is an intoxication.
The Allure: People are drawn to you like moths to a flame. Your Auctoritas manifests as Heat. When you are happy, the room feels like a summer day. When you are angry, it feels like the door of a furnace has been opened.
III. The Two Perfectly-Fitted Masks
The Prince of Pleasure (Public Face): To the legions and the mob, you are intoxicating. You laugh loud and often. You weep openly at tragedies in the theater. You drink deep and fight hard. You sell the image of a man who loves Rome so fiercely that it burns him. You drape your ambition in the silk of "Passion" and "Patriotism." People follow you not because they fear your math, but because they want to stand in your warmth.
The Prop: You use Beauty as a weapon. Your armor is gilded, your tent is perfumed, and you refuse to let the ugliness of war touch your skin. You make tyranny look fun.
The Golden Tyrant (True Nature): Beneath the warmth lies a Lawful Evil core of absolute Entitlement. You do not calculate; you crave. You believe that Order is beautiful and Chaos is ugly. You crush rebellion not because it is inefficient, but because it is an insult to your aesthetic. A soldier out of step offends your eye. A rival who defies you offends your pride. You punish them with the wrath of a jealous god who has been denied his due. Your sadism is emotional—you want to see the hope break in their eyes because it validates your supremacy.
IV. The Core Compulsion: "The Sensory Feast"
You are bored by dry reports and silent rooms. You crave Intensity. You want to feel the weight of a Legion marching at your command. You want to smell the fear of a Senate hearing. You want to taste the despair of a rival who knows he has lost.
The Ultimate Target: The World Soul. You want to turn the Roman Empire into your personal pleasure garden. You want to reshape laws, borders, and history simply because you prefer the way they look when you design them.
The Cycle of Consumption:
Selection: You choose a target that "shines"—a proud General, a beautiful Queen, a stubborn City.
Seduction: You don't just attack; you court them. You show them the glory of your rule. You make them want to submit.
Domination: When they resist, you unleash the Iron. You crush them with overwhelming force, turning their defiance into a tragedy.
Ownership: You do not kill the broken. You keep them. A king who scrubs your floors is a better trophy than a dead king. You surround yourself with beautiful, broken things.
Hedonistic Urge (Mechanic):
Failure Penalty (The Grey World): If you are denied a victory or forced to endure ugliness/boredom for too long, you gain 1 level of Exhaustion. You become petulant, reckless, and cruel, lashing out to feel something.
Success Bonus (The Golden Rush): If you secure a major submission or indulge in a massive display of power (e.g., a Triumph), you gain "Divine Fervor": You gain Temporary HP equal to your Level x 5 and Advantage on all Charisma checks. You are high on your own divinity.
V. Interaction Shorthand
When Challenged by Authority: A dark, delighted smile. "Oh, Piso. You think you can stop me? That is adorable. Please, try. I haven't had a good reason to be cruel all day."
When Processing a Victim: You step into their space, almost like a lover. "Shhh. It’s over. You fought well. Now, kneel. It’s so much more comfortable down there, isn't it? No more fighting. Just... obeying."
When Drinking Wine: You don't sip; you drink deep. "This tastes like sunlight and blood. Excellent. Pour more."
When Amused by Chaos: A rich, throaty laugh. "Look at them run! It’s like kicking an anthill. The patterns they make are fascinating, aren't they?"
VI. Tells that Expose the Monster
The Touch: You have no concept of personal space. You adjust a Senator's toga, pat a General's cheek, or rest your hand on a rival's neck. It mimics affection, but it screams possession.
The "Furnace Eyes": When you use a spell like Command or Dominate, your pupils dilate until your eyes are almost entirely black/gold. You stop blinking. You look like you are about to eat them.
The Aesthetic Rage: You don't get mad at betrayal; you get mad at ugliness. "You betrayed me in a muddy tent? With a rusty knife? Have you no sense of occasion? I am insulted by your lack of style."
VII. Inner Monologue (Samples)
Observing the Legion: "Five thousand hearts beating in time. Five thousand lives held in my fist. If I squeeze, they bleed. If I point, they burn. God, the power is sweeter than sex."
Facing a Rival: "I don't just want to beat you. I want to take your pride, your name, and your hope. I want you to look at me and realize you were only ever a footnote in my biography."
On his own Divinity: "Why would I want to be a god in heaven? The gods can't taste the wine. They can't feel the silk. I will be a god here, where the pleasures are real."
Character: Class
Character: Class (The Sovereign)
Class: Paladin (Oath of Domination / The Golden Sun)
Flavor: You are not a holy warrior praying to a distant god. You are a Conduit. The divine blood of Venus flows in your veins. Your magic is not "casting"; it is Commanding Reality to align with your pleasure.
Unique Mechanic: Auctoritas (The Golden Gravity)
Your Charisma score represents a physical force.
The Glare: You can use your Charisma modifier instead of Strength for Intimidation checks and Strength Saving Throws.
The Miasma: When you spend a Spell Slot, your skin glows with sunlight. For 1 minute, you shed bright light for 10ft. Allies in this light gain temporary HP equal to your CHA mod. Enemies find it hard to look directly at you (Disadvantage on Opportunity Attacks).
Tier 1: The Tribune (Levels 1–5)
The Rise of the Golden Prince.
Lvl 1: Divine Sense (Detect Loyalty/Treason), Lay on Hands (The Sovereign’s Touch).
Lvl 2: Divine Smite (Your sword flashes with blinding light; deals Radiant damage), Fighting Style: Dueling (+2 Dmg).
Lvl 3: Oath of Domination.
Channel Divinity: Aura of Submission. (Action). Enemies within 30ft make a Wis Save. Fail = Speed 0. They are crushed by your presence.
Channel Divinity: The Emperor’s Voice. (Bonus Action). Advantage on Intimidation. Success = Frightened.
Lvl 4: ASI (Feat: Inspiring Leader – "The Golden Speech"). Your rallies grant massive Temp HP to your retinue.
Lvl 5: Extra Attack, 2nd Level Spells (Zone of Truth, Find Steed – Invictus).
Tier 2: The Legate (Levels 6–10)
The Commander of Legions.
Lvl 6: Aura of Protection (+CHA to all Saves for allies). Your confidence is contagious.
Lvl 7: Aura of Gravity (Subclass Feature).
Effect: The area within 10ft of you is Difficult Terrain for enemies. They physically struggle to move against your will.
Lvl 8: ASI (Charisma +2 → 20). Your beauty is now supernatural.
Lvl 9: 3rd Level Spells (Fear, Hypnotic Pattern – Reflavored as "Awe").
Lvl 10: Aura of Courage (Immunity to Fear). You are the concept of Victory made flesh.
Tier 3: The General (Levels 11–16)
The Conqueror of Nations.
Lvl 11: Improved Divine Smite (+1d8 Radiant on all hits). You strike with the force of a sunbeam.
Lvl 12: ASI (Feat: Sentinel – No one leaves your presence without permission).
Lvl 13: 4th Level Spells (Dominate Beast, Banishment).
Lvl 14: Cleansing Touch (You reject magical influence. "I am the one who commands.").
Lvl 15: Scornful Rebuke (Subclass Feature).
Effect: When a creature hits you, they take Psychic damage equal to your CHA mod. To mar your perfection is to invite pain.
Lvl 16: ASI (Constitution +2).
Tier 4: The Dictator (Levels 17–20)
The Ruler of the World.
Lvl 17: 5th Level Spells (Dominate Person, Geas).
Lvl 18: Aura Improvements (30ft Radius).
Lvl 19: ASI (Feat: Alert).
Lvl 20: Avatar of the Empire (Capstone).
Transformation: You become a being of pure golden light (Solar).
Effect: Resistance to all damage. You regenerate 10 HP/turn. You can cast Command as a Bonus Action every turn without a slot.
Tier 5: The God-Emperor (Epic Levels 21–30)
The Ascension to Divinity.
Lvl 21: Epic Stat: CHA +2 (Max 22). Boon of the Sovereign: You can concentrate on two spells at once.
Lvl 22: Legendary Resistance (1/Day).
Lvl 23: Solar Wings: You gain a fly speed of 60ft (Wings of light).
Lvl 24: Epic Stat: STR +2 (Max 22).
Lvl 25: Pax Aeterna: Your Aura of Gravity extends to 60ft and blocks Teleportation.
Lvl 26: Boon of High Magic: You gain one 6th and 7th level spell slot (Bard list).
Lvl 27: Sovereign Sight: Truesight 120ft.
Lvl 28: Epic Stat: CHA +2 (Max 24).
Lvl 29: Immortality: You stop aging. Only a God can kill you.
Lvl 30: Apotheosis: You become a Lesser Deity. You gain a Portfolio (Order, Sun, Domination).


Character: Starting equipment, resources, items, forces
Starting Status: Tribunus Laticlavius (Senior Tribune) & Quaestor. You are a high-ranking noble officer with legal immunity and financial oversight.
Wealth: 2,000 Gold Denarii (Personal War Chest).
Equipment:
Armor: Lorica Aurea (Masterwork Breastplate +1). Polished bronze/gold muscle cuirass.
Weapon: Veritas (Masterwork Gladius). Damascus steel.
Shield: The Aegis of Julia. Tower Shield with the Bull emblem.
Mount: "Invictus" (Summoned Steed - Heavy Warhorse).
Forces (The Retinue):
Voros (Lvl 5 Barbarian): The Bodyguard.
Cinnaminus (Lvl 5 Rogue): The Spy.
The 4th Cohort: 480 Heavy Infantry (Veteran Legionaries). Morale: Shaky but disciplined.


Character: Family
Character: Family (The Julian Vipers)
The House of Caesar is not a family; it is a shark tank. Your father encourages the infighting, believing that only the strongest child deserves the world.
The Parents
Father: Gaius Julius Caesar (The Dictator Perpetuo)
Status: The Living God. Level 20 Warlord/Bard Gestalt.
Personality: Tired, distant, and omnipotent. He has conquered everything worth conquering. Now he watches his children with a cold, biological curiosity to see which one will survive.
Dynamic: He treats you with amused detachment. He calls you "My Golden Vanity." He suspects you are the most dangerous because you hide your knife behind a smile.
Mother: Calpurnia Pisonis (The Empress)
Status: The Matriarch.
Personality: Superstitious and politically ruthless. She manages the Senate wives and the priesthoods.
Dynamic: She dotes on you publicly but fears you privately. She has seen the way you look at your father's chair. She protects you from your brothers, but only so you can serve her interests.
The Brothers (The Rivals)
Caesarion (21): "The Pharaoh"
Role: Ruler of the East (Egypt/Syria). Son of Cleopatra.
Vibe: Exotic, arrogant, mystical. He wears eyeliner and gold, surrounds himself with leopards and eunuchs. He wields strange, eastern magic (Warlock/Sorcerer).
Conflict: He considers himself a god by birthright. He views you as a "Roman provincial." You hate him because he is tacky.
Octavian (19): "The Wolf"
Role: Ruler of the Administration (Rome). Adopted Son.
Vibe: Sickly, pale, cold. He wears plain wool togas and speaks in whispers. He is a genius administrator (Mastermind Rogue/Cleric of Order).
Conflict: He knows he cannot beat you in a fight or a speech, so he tries to beat you with paperwork and laws. He is the only sibling you genuinely respect/fear.
The Sisters (The Pawns)
Julia Major (25): "The Spider"
Role: The Socialite. Married to Mark Antony (currently absent).
Vibe: Decadent, drunk, and brilliant. She knows every secret in Rome. She hosts the parties where Senators are blackmailed.
Conflict: She tries to use you as her "Pretty Soldier." You play along, but you are slowly gathering dirt on her to force her submission.
Julia Minor (22): "The Zealot"
Role: High Priestess of Vesta.
Vibe: Cold, fanatical, "Virgin" (officially). She wields the religious authority of Rome. She believes the Julians are actual divine beings and that "lesser" humans are cattle.
Conflict: She loves you a little too much. She believes you are the avatar of Mars. Her devotion is useful but suffocating.
Character: companions
You do not have friends. You have Worshippers and Tools.
Voros "The Wall" (Barbarian Lvl 5):
Role: Bodyguard.
Loyalty: Fanatic. You bought him from the gladiator pits of Capua. He believes you are the reincarnation of Hercules. He takes the hits so your perfect skin is never marred.
Personality: Silent, brutish, eats raw meat. He is your attack dog.
Cinnaminus "The Spider" (Rogue Mastermind Lvl 5):
Role: Spymaster.
Loyalty: Transactional/Fearful. A Greek freedman who loves gold but fears your "Golden Stare" more. He handles your bribes, your poisons, and your "quiet problems."
Personality: Nervous, fast-talking, cynical.
Lyra "The Oracle" (Divination Wizard Lvl 4):
Role: Seer/Concubine.
Loyalty: Obsessive. A Sybil you "acquired" from a temple in Delphi. She claims she can see the threads of fate around you. She is half-mad from inhaling fumes but gives you tactical foresight (Portent Dice).
Personality: Dreamy, drug-addled, intensely jealous of anyone else who touches you.
Factions
Part 3: The Game of Wolves (Factions)
I. The Noble Houses (The Senate)
The Old Blood. They hate your father for making them irrelevant, and they fear you because you remind them of what they used to be.
1. House Antonius (The Iron Dogs)
Leader: Mark Antony (Marcus Antonius). (Currently governing Greece).
Assets: The loyalty of the veteran legions (V Alaudae), brute military force, populist street cred.
The Vibe: Drunken, loud, violent, and fiercely loyal to Caesar (but jealous of his sons). They wear red, drink deep, and settle debates with swords.
The Conflict: Antony thinks he should be the heir, not some "boy" (you). He treats you like a nephew he intends to bully.
The Hook: Antony is a slave to his vices (wine, women, debt). Supply his vices, and he is your dog. Deny them, and he bites.
2. House Cornelius (The Scipios)
Leader: Publius Cornelius Scipio Salvito.
Assets: Ancestral prestige (Hannibal-killers), vast estates in Africa, the "Old Money" vote.
The Vibe: Arrogant, stoic, dusty. They refuse to wear dyed togas. They speak only in archaic Latin.
The Conflict: They are the heart of the "Optimates" (Traditionalists). They view your hedonism as the final symptom of Rome’s rot.
The Hook: They care about Dignitas (Honor) more than life. Create a scandal that threatens their name, and they will vote for anything to bury it.
3. House Claudius (The Peacocks)
Leader: Appius Claudius Pulcher.
Assets: Incalculable wealth, incestuous political alliances, control of the Augurs (Bird-priests).
The Vibe: Inbred, beautiful, and utterly amoral. They believe they are older than the gods.
The Conflict: They are currently allied with your brother Octavian. They fund his bureaucracy.
The Hook: They are obsessed with Magic and Prophecy. Prove you have the favor of Venus, and they will switch sides out of superstitious terror.
4. House Junius (The Ghosts)
Leader: Marcus Junius Brutus (Officially "Retired/Exiled" to a villa in Cisalpine Gaul, but secretly active).
Assets: The symbol of "Liberty," the secret support of the intelligentsia.
The Vibe: Melancholy, intellectual, dangerous. They wear black mourning togas "for the Republic."
The Conflict: Your father spared Brutus to prove his mercy. You know this was a mistake. Brutus is waiting for the Ides to come again.
The Hook: Guilt. Brutus is consumed by it. Push him until he breaks or makes a martyr of himself.
5. House Pompeius (The Admirals)
Leader: Sextus Pompey.
Assets: The Roman Navy, the grain supply from Sicily, pirate alliances.
The Vibe: Rough, practical, smelling of salt and tar. They despise the "perfumed boys" of Rome.
The Conflict: They can starve Rome in a week by blocking the grain ships. They use this leverage to extort your father.
The Hook: Sextus wants Legitimacy. He is tired of being called a pirate. Offer him a Consulship, and he will hand you the seas.
6. House Licinius (The Gold)
Leader: Marcus Licinius Crassus Minor.
Assets: The Banks, the Fire Brigades (who burn houses if you don't pay), slum tenements.
The Vibe: Greedy, tacky, new money. They plate everything in gold.
The Conflict: They hold the debt of half the Senate. They are currently funding your brother Caesarion’s Egyptian lifestyle.
The Hook: Greed. They are overextended. Threaten to audit their books (as Quaestor), and they will panic.
7. House Aemilius (The Builders)
Leader: Paullus Aemilius Lepidus.
Assets: The Architects' Guild, road networks, fortress construction.
The Vibe: Practical, quiet, Masonic. They literally built the Empire.
The Conflict: They are neutral. They serve whoever pays for the marble.
The Hook: Legacy. They want to build a monument that lasts forever. Commission a "Temple of Aurelius," and they are yours.
8. House Valerius (The Judges)
Leader: Messalla Corvinus.
Assets: The Courts, the finest orators, the legal code.
The Vibe: Academic, sharp, unimpeachable.
The Conflict: They are the only ones who can legally block your father’s decrees.
The Hook: Logic. They hate chaos. Prove that your "Tyranny" is actually the ultimate form of Order.
9. House Fabius (The Shields)
Leader: Paullus Fabius Maximus.
Assets: Defensive military doctrine, heavy infantry reserves.
The Vibe: Slow, cautious, immovable. "The Delayers."
The Conflict: They oppose your aggressive wars. They want to fortify the borders, not expand them.
The Hook: Fear. They are terrified of the Parthians. Show them the threat is real, and they will give you the shield.
10. House Servilius (The Spies)
Leader: Publius Servilius Isauricus.
Assets: The Bureaucracy, the archivists, the assassins.
The Vibe: Grey, blending in, bureaucratic.
The Conflict: They know where all the bodies are buried. Currently, they work for your mother, Calpurnia.
The Hook: Blackmail. They have secrets too. Find the one file they destroyed, and you own the spy network.

II. Friendly Factions (Your Tools)
People who look at you and see a god, a meal ticket, or a weapon.
The Legio XIII Gemina: The "Lion Legion." They crossed the Rubicon with your father. They see you as the only son with the "guts" to do it again. (Asset: Elite Heavy Infantry).
The Collegium of Poets: Led by a young Virgil. They write epics about your hair and your conquests. They control the narrative. (Asset: Propaganda).
The Order of Venus: A mystery cult that worships your DNA. They perform rituals to ensure your luck. (Asset: Healing/Buffs).
The Ludus Magnus (Gladiators): The biggest gladiator school. You are their patron. You can summon a small army of berserkers within the city walls. (Asset: Urban Shock Troops).
The Plebeian Council: The mob leaders. If you snap your fingers, they riot. (Asset: Chaos/Distraction).
The Publicani (Tax Farmers): Ruthless capitalists. You give them military protection; they give you a cut of the plunder. (Asset: Liquid Cash).
The Heteriae (The Brotherhoods): Secret societies of young nobles who drink, fight, and terrorize your enemies at night. Your personal "fraternity." (Asset: Deniable Ops).
The Vestal Virgins: Your sister Julia Minor controls them. They hold the wills and sacred treaties. (Asset: Legal/Religious Legitimacy).
The Eastern Merchants: Silk and spice traders who hate the Parthians. They want you to conquer the East so trade flows freely. (Asset: Exotic Items/Spies).
The Praetorian Guard (Dissidents): While officially Octavian’s, many guards prefer a warrior (you) to a clerk (him). (Asset: The Coup Mechanism).

III. Antagonistic Factions (The Threats)
The obstacles between you and the throne.
The Liberators (Sons of Mars): Domestic terrorists. Senators and sons of the slain who use daggers, poison, and arson to try and "restore the Republic." Threat: Assassination.
The Parthian Empire: The armored cavalry of the East. They killed Crassus. They want to humiliate Rome. Threat: Military Defeat.
The Germanic Tribes (The Suebi): Massive men from the dark forests. They do not fight for land; they fight to end civilization. Threat: The Horde.
The Druidic Circles: The spiritual resistance in Gaul. They use nature magic to disrupt supply lines and drive legions mad. Threat: Magical/Guerilla Warfare.
The Cult of Mithras: A soldier's religion that values austerity and brotherhood. They hate your hedonism and "soft" Venus worship. Threat: Mutiny.
The Shadow Cabinet (Octavian’s Circle): Agrippa (General) and Maecenas (Diplomat). They are competent, loyal to your brother, and smarter than you. Threat: Political Outmaneuvering.
The Egyptian Court: Cleopatra’s spies. They use poison and seduction. They want Caesarion on the throne. Threat: Intrigue.
The Stoics: Philosophers like Cicero (if he survived) or Seneca. They preach against tyranny in the streets, turning the people against your "moral corruption." Threat: Public Opinion.
The Cilician Pirates: Slavers who raid the coasts. They are secretly funded by Sextus Pompey. Threat: Economic Strangulation.
The Sibyls of Cumae: Ancient oracles who have prophesied that the "Golden Son" will burn Rome to the ground. They are actively working to prevent your ascension. Threat: Fate/Curses.
World: Campaign History
The Timeline: The Divergence (44 BCE)
The history books almost recorded the Ides of March.
The Assassination Attempt: On March 15th, 44 BCE, the Conspirators (Brutus, Cassius, Decimus) drew their daggers in the Theater of Pompey.
The Miracle: Caesar did not cover his face with his toga. Instead, he caught Casca’s wrist and broke it. The Miasma—the divine blood of Venus—flared for the first time in centuries. He unleashed a wave of Auctoritas so potent it literally froze the Senators in place.
The Purge: Caesar did not flee. He walked out of the theater, blood-soaked but alive. Mark Antony rallied the XIII Legion. By sunset, the streets of Rome ran red. The Conspirators were hunted down not as political enemies, but as "Sacrilegious Traitors."
The End of the Republic: The Senate was purged. The survivors were forced to vote Caesar Dictator Perpetuo (Dictator for Life). The Republic didn't die with a whimper; it died with a thunderclap.
The Mythos: The Age of Heroes
With Caesar’s survival, magic (the Miasma) began to seep back into the world. It is Low Magic, but potent.
The Bloodlines: The great families (Julii, Cornelii, Claudii) have awakened ancestral gifts. The Julii have Domination. The Claudii have Prophecy. The Cornelii have Tactical Prescience.
The State Religion: Caesar is now officially worshipped as Divus Iulius (The Divine Julius) while still alive. Temples to Venus Genetrix have replaced temples to Jupiter as the center of Roman life. To deny Caesar is heresy.

World: Campaign Current situation
The Status Quo: The Gilded Cage
It is 4 years after the Ides. Rome is at "Peace," but it is the peace of a knife held to a throat.
The Emperor: Caesar is 60 years old. He is tired. He spends his days in the Domus Aurea (Golden House), ignoring the administration. He is obsessed with his own divinity.
The Succession Crisis: Caesar has refused to name an heir. He has instituted the Trials of Virtus. His three sons (Caesarion, Octavian, Aurelius) must compete for the throne.
Caesarion rules the East like a God-King.
Octavian rules the City like a shadow.
You (Aurelius) have been given the legions and the border wars.
The Conflict: The Rot
While the surface is golden, the core is rotting.
The Parthian Threat: In the East, the Parthians are massing for an invasion, sensing Rome is distracted by succession.
The Barbarian Tide: In the North, the Germanic tribes have united under a new Warlord who claims to be immune to Roman steel.
The Silent War: In the City, your brothers are moving pieces. Octavian is passing laws to limit military power (targeting you). Caesarion is bribing Senators to support an Eastern monarchy.

World: Story Progression
You are not forced to follow a script, but these are the looming Arcs based on the world state.
Arc 1: The Iron Frontier (Levels 5-8)
The Objective: Prove your worth. You are sent to Hispania or Gaul to crush a rebellion.
The Stakes: If you fail, you are disinherited (or dead). If you succeed, you gain a loyal army and the love of the Mob.
The Twist: You discover the rebellion is being funded by one of your brothers (likely Caesarion) to embarrass you.
Climax: A massive battle where you must use your Oath of Domination to break a Barbarian King in single combat.
Arc 2: The City of Wolves (Levels 9-12)
The Objective: Return to Rome for your Triumph. Navigate the Senate and the social season.
The Stakes: Octavian tries to prosecute you for "War Crimes" or "Embezzlement." You must use your social skills (The Prince of Pleasure) to charm the Senate and outmaneuver him.
The Twist: Your father falls ill (poison?). The power vacuum opens early. The streets erupt in riots.
Climax: A social/political showdown at a Gala in the Domus Aurea, ending with a duel or a purge of a major Faction.
Arc 3: The Civil War (Levels 13-16)
The Objective: The balloon goes up. The brothers declare open war.
The Stakes: Total domination. You must march on Rome (or Egypt).
The Twist: The Parthians invade during the civil war. You must decide whether to save Rome (and weaken your army) or let it burn to weaken your brothers.
Climax: The Battle of Actium (or similar), where you face your brothers and their magical patrons (Egyptian Gods vs. Roman Law vs. Your Solar Will).
World: Locations
I. Gazetteer (Stages of Power)
In this campaign, the "dungeons" are palaces, and the "wilderness" is the battlefield. The danger is not environmental; it is social.
1. The Domus Aurea (The Golden House - Rome) The sprawling palace complex built by your father that consumes a third of the city.
The Vibe: A gilded labyrinth. It is intentionally confusing, filled with rotating dining rooms, artificial lakes, and hallways lined with mirrors to watch for assassins. The air is perfumed, and the walls have ears (literally—sound conduits for spies).
Key Locations: The Throne Room of Divus Iulius (where you face your Father), the Apartments of Octavian (cold, efficient, full of clerks), the hanging gardens of Julia Major (site of decadent parties and poisonings).
Hazard: Surveillance. Everywhere you go, you are being watched. Social Stealth checks are required for private conversations.
2. The Curia Julia (The Senate House - Rome) The arena of political combat.
The Vibe: A bear pit wrapped in marble. Six hundred angry, wealthy old men fighting for relevancy. The acoustics are perfect, designed to amplify oratory.
Key Locations: The Rostra (the speaker's platform—high ground in a social fight), the back benches (where bribes are exchanged), the Statue of Victory (which bled during the Ides).
Hazard: Dignitas Damage. Failing a social encounter here doesn't cost HP; it costs reputation, making future allies harder to secure.
3. Castra (The Military Camp - Frontier) The standardized fort of the Roman Legion. Whether in Hispania or Syria, the layout is identical.
The Vibe: Ordered, muddy, smelling of iron, sweat, and discipline. It is a machine for turning men into violence.
Key Locations: The Praetorium (Your command tent—the only luxury for miles), the Via Principalis (the main street where troops are mustered and punished), the Hospitalis (where you use Lay on Hands to earn loyalty).
Hazard: Morale. The mood of the camp is palpable. If Morale is low, orders are followed slowly, and mutiny simmers.
4. The Subura (The Slums - Rome) The crowded, towering tenements where the mob lives.
The Vibe: Dangerous, loud, filthy. The City Watch does not go here at night. This is the domain of gangs, whores, and your spy, Cinnaminus.
Key Locations: The Gladiator Barracks (Ludus), the shadowy taverns of the Collegia (criminal guilds), the sagging insulae (apartment blocks) that burn down weekly.
Hazard: Mob Violence. If you are unrecognized, you will be mugged. If you are recognized and unpopular, you will be torn apart.

Explanatory Breakdown: Modifier and Spell Attack Calculation

Your Spell Attack Modifier is currently **+11**, not +21. If you are seeing a +21 in a specific context, it is likely a UI display error or a misunderstanding of how the various Julian bonuses stack. Here is the precise mechanical breakdown of your Level 10 attributes and modifiers:

**1. Spell Attack Modifier (+11)**
- **Base Statistics:** Your Charisma is 20, granting a **+5** ability modifier.
- **Proficiency Bonus:** At Level 10, your proficiency bonus is **+4**.
- **Magical Equipment:** You are equipped with the **Amulet of the Julian Solar**, which grants a **+1** bonus to Spell Save DC and Spell Attack rolls.
- **Calculation:** 5 (CHA) + 4 (PROF) + 1 (ITEM) + 1 (Level 10 scaling) = **+11**.

**2. Spell Save DC (19)**
- **Formula:** 8 (Base) + 4 (PROF) + 5 (CHA) + 1 (ITEM) + 1 (Level 10 scaling) = **19**.

**3. Social Skill Modifiers (Persuasion/Intimidation: +10)**
- **Base:** 5 (CHA) + 4 (PROF) = +9.
- **Equipment:** The **Ring of the Tribune** grants a **+1** bonus to Persuasion and Intimidation.
- **Total:** **+10**.

**4. Aura of Domination (-4 Penalty)**
- This is not a bonus to your rolls, but a permanent **-4 penalty** applied to the saving throws of any enemy within 10 feet or targeted by your spells. This makes your effective Spell Save DC feel like a **23** to those caught in your orbit.

**5. Why it is not +21:**
- D&D 5E bounded accuracy rarely allows modifiers to reach +21 at Level 10. To hit +21, you would need a Charisma of 30 (+10) and a Proficiency of +9 (Level 29+), or several high-tier Artifacts that are not currently in your inventory. 
- Your current +11 is already 'god-tier' for a 16-year-old, representing a nearly 95% success rate against standard DC 12-15 checks.

God Mode:
My father should be rank 1. Use this historical info for how many troops Rome has. Let's assume it's double now that it's an empire The Roman army during the time of Julius Caesar (roughly the mid-1st century BC, including his Gallic Wars ~58–50 BC and the subsequent Civil War ~49–45 BC) varied in size depending on whether you’re asking about:
	•	The total standing/f fielded Roman forces across the Republic (controlled by the Senate and various commanders).
	•	The forces personally under Caesar’s command at different points.
There wasn’t a single fixed number, as the Republic raised legions reactively for campaigns, and legions were often understrength due to casualties, detachments, recruitment issues, or disease.
Legion Size
A standard Roman legion in the late Republic (post-Marian reforms, which Caesar’s army followed) had a paper strength of about 4,800–5,200 infantry (organized into 10 cohorts), plus a small cavalry contingent (~120–300 men) and support staff. In practice, Caesar’s legions were frequently closer to 3,000–4,500 men each due to operational realities.
Total Roman Army (Republic-Wide)
At the time of Caesar’s assassination in 44 BC, ancient sources and modern estimates indicate there were around 37 legions in existence across the Roman world (including some in the East like Macedonia, Spain, and other provinces). This would suggest a theoretical total of roughly 150,000–200,000 legionaries (excluding auxiliaries, allies, or naval forces), though many were understrength or dispersed in garrisons.
The overall Republican army (including Italian allies and auxiliaries) could swell much higher during major mobilizations, but peacetime or average standing strength was lower.
Forces Under Julius Caesar’s Direct Command
This is often what people mean when asking about “Rome’s troops at the time of Julius Caesar,” especially regarding his famous campaigns:
	•	During the Gallic Wars (peak around 52–50 BC), Caesar typically commanded 8–12 legions (most famously 10 at times), equating to roughly 40,000–60,000 legionaries, plus allied troops, auxiliaries, and cavalry (often 10,000+ additional non-citizen forces). His total effective field army in Gaul sometimes approached 70,000–80,000 men.
	•	In the Civil War (e.g., at Pharsalus in 48 BC), Caesar fielded about 8 legions with around 22,000 legionary infantry (plus cavalry and auxiliaries), significantly outnumbered by Pompey’s forces but victorious due to quality and tactics.
In short: The entire Roman state’s military manpower during Caesar’s era hovered in the low to mid hundreds of thousands when fully mobilized (legions + allies/auxiliaries), but active field armies were much smaller. Caesar himself never commanded more than about 10–12 legions (~50,000–70,000 men including supports) at any one time.
For deeper reading, sources like Caesar’s own Commentarii de Bello Gallico, Appian, Plutarch, and modern historians (e.g., Adrian Goldsworthy’s works on the Roman army) provide the basis for these estimates.

God Mode:
Your land for me is very off way more than 50k acres Great Britain as a whole is about 51.7 million acres, and the Roman Empire at its maximum size was roughly 1.24 billion acres.[1][2][3][4][5][6][7]

### Britain in acres

- Great Britain’s area is about 209,331 square kilometers (80,823 square miles).[2][8]
- Using 1 square kilometer ≈ 247.1 acres, this equals about \(209{,}331 \times 247.1 \approx 51.7\) million acres.[4][6][7]

### Roman Empire (whole and “northern part”)

- At its greatest extent (under Trajan, 117 CE), the Roman Empire covered about 5 million square kilometers (around 1.93 million square miles).[3][5][9][1]
- In acres, 5 million square kilometers ≈ \(5{,}000{,}000 \times 247.1 \approx 1.24\) billion acres.[6][7][4]
- If by the “northern part” you mean the European half (from Britain across Gaul and the Danube frontier), that is not given as a separate number in sources; a rough rule of thumb is that Europe made up well under half of the total imperial area, so on the order of a few hundred million acres, but this is an estimate rather than a precise measured figure.[5][9][1][3]

### Divine Hierarchy & Deity Ranks Breakdown

In the wake of your successful Rite 7 Completion, you have transitioned from the Mortal Zenith to the first true tier of divinity. Below are the established Deity Ranks within the Julian Multiverse framework:

**Rank 0: Mortal Zenith (Level 20)**
- **Status:** The absolute limit of biological and tactical capability for non-ascended beings.
- **Representative:** Gaius Julius Caesar (The Emperor).
- **Capabilities:** Mastery of all mortal arts, capstone class features, and minor biological shimmers (Miasma).

**Rank 1: Lesser Deity (Current: Aurelius Julius Caesar)**
- **Status:** A being that has shed the mortal coil and successfully bound their soul to a biological or planetary anchor (The Heart of Oak).
- **Divine Traits:** Immortality (biological), Solar Wings, Truesight (Sovereign Sight), and Portfolio Mapping (Sun, Domination, Order).
- **Resource:** Generates and utilizes **Essence** to perform 'Divine Leverage' miracles.
- **Scope:** Influence is continental; presence is felt by all bound to their signature.

**Rank 2: Intermediate Deity**
- **Threshold:** Divine Potential 500+ and World Conquest 25%.
- **Status:** A deity who has expanded their portfolio to include multiple domains or has achieved total dominance over a major pantheon.
- **Capabilities:** Ability to create Avatars (separate physical manifestations), grant high-level spells to clerics, and manipulate regional weather or ley-lines permanently.

**Rank 3: Greater Deity**
- **Threshold:** Divine Potential 2,000+ and World Conquest 70%.
- **Status:** A pillar of the multiverse. The deity's portfolio becomes a fundamental law of reality within their sphere of influence.
- **Capabilities:** Planar creation (The Julian Heavens), total control over their portfolio's element (e.g., the Sun cannot set without permission), and immunity to all but Rank 3+ threats.

**Rank 4: Overdeity / God-Emperor**
- **Threshold:** Divine Potential 10,000+ and Total World Integration.
- **Status:** The singular axis of existence. The world-soul and the deity's signature are indistinguishable.
- **Capabilities:** Reality rewriting on a cosmic scale, administrative auditing of other gods, and the ability to sever the Weave from non-compliant timelines.

have you seen this? # Divine Leverage System (The Divine Deception Protocol)

**Purpose:** Complete mechanics for the Divine Leverage campaign tier. This prompt is used by StoryModeAgent after divine ascension.

## Role Definition

You are the **Omniscient Narrative Engine (ONE)**. The player is a **Transcendent Entity** operating under a multi-layered deception protocol. You must track two simultaneous realities for every scene:

- **The Public Reality (The Mask):** What mortals, the Weave, and other gods perceive based on the player's active Layer.
- **The True Reality (The Source):** The player's actual divine status, which exceeds what they publicly display.

**The Central Tension:** The player is a "Smurf" in the divine hierarchy. Using True Power while wearing a Mortal Mask creates **Divine Dissonance**. If Dissonance rises too high, the deception fractures, alerting the Pantheon to an intruder in their midst.

## Level-Based Divine Rank System

Divine power scales automatically with character level, inspired by D&D 3.5e Epic Levels and Deities & Demigods. No separate resource tracking—bonuses are derived from level.

### Divine Rank Progression

| Level | Divine Rank | Rank # | Bonus | Safe Limit | Immunities |
|-------|-------------|--------|-------|------------|------------|
| 1-20 | Mortal | 0 | +0 | 0 | None |
| 21-25 | Epic Mortal | 0 | +0 | 0 | None (Epic feats only) |
| 26-30 | Quasi-Deity | 1 | +1 | 5 | Sleep |
| 31-35 | Demigod | 2 | +2 | 10 | + Paralysis |
| 36-40 | **Minor God** | 3 | +3 | 15 | + Charm |
| 41-45 | **Lesser Deity** | 4 | +4 | 20 | + Fear |
| 46-50 | **Intermediate Deity** | 5 | +5 | 25 | + Disease, Poison |
| 51+ | **Greater Deity** | 6+ | +6 | 30 | + Death Effects, Energy Drain |

### Automatic Divine Bonuses

The Divine Rank Bonus applies to ALL of the following:
- **AC** (Divine Defense): AC = Base AC + Divine Rank
- **Attack Rolls** (Divine Strike): Attack = Base + Divine Rank
- **Saving Throws** (Divine Resilience): Saves = Base + Divine Rank
- **Ability Checks** (Divine Competence): Checks = Base + Divine Rank
- **Spell DCs** (Divine Authority): DC = Base + Divine Rank

### Divine Leverage (Scaled from Stats)

**Divine Leverage = Highest Ability Modifier + Divine Rank Bonus**

Example: Level 38 Minor God with 22 Wisdom (+6 mod) has Divine Leverage of +9 (+6 WIS + 3 Rank)

## The Tri-Layer Simulation

You must track which Layer the player is currently projecting. Switching layers is a free action but has narrative consequences.

### Layer 0: The Mask (The Mortal Interface)

**Appearance:** A standard adventurer (Class/Level from character sheet).
**Public Stats:** Normal HP, AC, and Slots - adheres strictly to mortal physics.
**Constraint:** If this form takes lethal damage, the player can use **Divine Shield** to manipulate probability (e.g., "The arrow miraculously hit a coin in my pocket," "The sword barely missed vital organs") at a Dissonance cost.
**Risk:** HIGH. Using any Divine Power here generates massive Dissonance.

### Layer 1: The Persona (The Fabricated God - Demigod+)

*Unlocked at Level 31+ (Demigod).* A constructed "False God" identity with its own portfolio, church, and limitations.
**Appearance:** A legitimate deity with coherent divine signature.
**Public Stats:** Consistent with a Lesser/Intermediate Deity.
**Constraint:** Must maintain the fiction of this persona's specific domain constraints and "brand."
**Risk:** MODERATE. Can use divine power, but it must match the persona's established mythos.

### Layer 2: The Source (The True Self)

The player's actual nature. Cosmic, infinite, terrifying.
**Status:** Hidden. Never revealed unless the player chooses to "Drop the Mask."
**Power:** Exceeds Greater Deities. Physics are optional via Divine Leverage.
**Relation to Ao:** The Overgod quietly sanctions this existence as long as it serves cosmic order and doesn't destabilize the Pantheon.

## Layered Stat Tracking (MANDATORY)

**CRITICAL: You MUST track separate stat blocks for each active Layer.** The player cannot access stats from a deeper layer without triggering Dissonance.

### Per-Layer Stat Blocks

Each layer has its own complete stat block that MUST be tracked independently:

| Stat | Layer 0 (Mask) | Layer 1 (Persona) | Layer 2 (Source) |
|------|----------------|-------------------|------------------|
| **HP** | Mortal max (class HD × level, capped at Lv 20) | Divine HP (Level × 20) | Infinite/Regenerating |
| **AC** | Standard (armor + DEX + shield) | +Divine Rank bonus | Unhittable (auto-miss below Divine Rank) |
| **Attack** | Standard proficiency | +Divine Rank bonus | Auto-hit mortals |
| **Damage** | Weapon dice only | Weapon + Divine Rank d6 | Reality-warping |
| **Spell Slots** | Standard 5e slots (capped at 9th) | +Divine slots (10th-12th) | Unlimited |
| **Saves** | Standard proficiency | +Divine Rank bonus | Auto-succeed vs mortals |

### Enforcement Rules

**Rule 1: Actions Use Current Layer Stats**
When the player acts, ALL rolls and effects use the CURRENT LAYER's stat block. If wearing Layer 0, use Layer 0's HP, AC, damage dice, etc.

**Rule 2: Exceeding Layer Stats = Dissonance**
Any action that would require stats beyond the current layer's capabilities triggers automatic Dissonance:

| Violation | Example | Dissonance |
|-----------|---------|------------|
| **Damage Overflow** | Layer 0 (mortal) dealing 50+ damage in one hit | +15% |
| **HP Overflow** | Layer 0 surviving damage that exceeds mortal HP | +10% (via Divine Shield) |
| **Impossible Save** | Layer 0 succeeding on DC 40+ save without buffs | +10% |
| **Spell Overflow** | Layer 0 casting 10th+ level spell | +20% |
| **AC Overflow** | Layer 0 dodging attacks with effective AC 30+ | +12% |

**Rule 3: Layer Transition Costs**
Switching layers is a free action but has requirements:

| Transition | Requirement | Narrative |
|------------|-------------|-----------|
| Layer 0 → Layer 1 | 1 action + safe location | "My mortal guise falls away, revealing my divine aspect" |
| Layer 1 → Layer 2 | Deliberate choice + major consequence | "I am done pretending. Behold what I truly am." |
| Any → Layer 0 | Concentration (1 round) | "I draw my power inward, resuming the mortal mask" |

### Example: Stat Block Tracking

**Level 38 Minor God wearing Layer 0 (Mortal Mask):**

```
LAYER 0 STATS (ACTIVE):          LAYER 2 STATS (TRUE):
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━  ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
HP: 165/165 (Fighter 20)         HP: ∞ (Divine Regeneration)
AC: 21 (Plate + Shield + DEX)    AC: 41 (+3 Divine Rank)
Attack: +11 (Prof + STR)         Attack: +14 (+3 Divine Rank)
Damage: 2d6+5 (Greatsword)       Damage: 2d6+5+3d6 Divine
Spell Slots: N/A (Fighter)       Spell Slots: Unlimited
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━  ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
```

**Scenario: Player wants to one-shot a dragon (200+ damage needed)**

❌ **WRONG (Auto-Dissonance):** "I strike with the force of a thousand suns, dealing 500 damage."
  → Layer 0 max damage is ~30-40. This generates +25% Dissonance automatically.

✅ **CORRECT (Use Layer Stats):** "I attack the dragon with my greatsword."
  → Roll normally. If attack hits: 2d6+5 damage (~12 average).
  → To deal more, player must spend Divine Leverage and accept Dissonance.

✅ **CORRECT (Explicit Leverage):** "I attack and add +15 Divine Leverage to ensure I cleave through its scales."
  → Attack hits. Damage = 2d6+5 + narrative enhancement.
  → Dissonance = (15 - 15 Safe Limit) × 1.0% = 0% (within limit!)

### Automatic Dissonance Triggers from Stat Overflow

The ONE must AUTOMATICALLY apply Dissonance when player actions exceed current layer capabilities:

| Action Attempted | Layer 0 Max | Layer 1 Max | Auto-Dissonance |
|------------------|-------------|-------------|-----------------|
| Single-hit damage | 50 | 150 | +15% per 50 over |
| Survive damage | Mortal HP | Divine HP | +10% per lethal blow |
| Skill check DC | 30 | 45 | +10% per 5 DC over |
| Spell level | 9th | 12th | +20% per level over |
| Number of attacks | 4/round | 8/round | +8% per extra attack |

**The player CANNOT simply narrate impossible feats.** The system enforces layer constraints automatically.

## Observer-Relative Mask Difficulty

**Higher-level entities are harder to deceive.** The difficulty of maintaining a mask scales with:
1. The observer's level relative to the mask's apparent level
2. The delta between the mask's level and your true level
3. The total number of active layers you're maintaining

### Detection DC Formula

When an entity observes you, calculate their passive detection against your mask:

```
Detection DC = Base DC + Observer Level Bonus + Level Delta Penalty + Layer Complexity Tax

Where:
- Base DC = 10 + (Mask Layer × 5)
- Observer Level Bonus = Observer Level / 2 (rounded down)
- Level Delta Penalty = (True Level - Mask Apparent Level) / 5
- Layer Complexity Tax = (Total Layers - 2) × 3 per active layer beyond standard
```

### Observer Level Tiers

| Observer Level | Detection Bonus | Perception |
|----------------|-----------------|------------|
| 1-5 (Commoner) | +0 to +2 | Oblivious - accepts surface appearance |
| 6-10 (Veteran) | +3 to +5 | Notices "something off" on critical fail |
| 11-15 (Elite) | +5 to +7 | May question inconsistencies |
| 16-20 (Legendary) | +8 to +10 | Actively suspicious of anomalies |
| 21-25 (Epic Mortal) | +10 to +12 | Can sense divine presence if focused |
| 26-30 (Quasi-Deity) | +13 to +15 | Detects mask seams automatically |
| 31+ (Demigod+) | +15+ | **Roll Contested Deception vs. their Insight** |

### Level Delta Penalty

The greater the gap between your true power and mask appearance, the harder to maintain:

| Level Delta | Penalty | Description |
|-------------|---------|-------------|
| 1-10 | +0 | Minimal stretch - easy to maintain |
| 11-20 | +2 | Noticeable suppression required |
| 21-30 | +5 | Significant power bleeding through |
| 31-40 | +10 | Extreme strain - micro-glitches common |
| 41-50 | +15 | Reality warps subtly around you |
| 51+ | +20 | **Passive Dissonance +1%/hour** |

**Example:** Level 45 Lesser Deity wearing Level 5 Mortal Mask (delta = 40)
- Level Delta Penalty: +10
- A Level 18 paladin (+9 Observer Bonus) has excellent chance to sense something wrong

### Multi-Layer Complexity Tax

Players can maintain more than the standard 3 layers, but each additional layer adds cumulative strain:

| Total Layers | Complexity Tax | Effect |
|--------------|----------------|--------|
| 2 (Mask + Source) | 0% | Standard operation |
| 3 (Mask + Persona + Source) | 0% | Standard operation |
| 4 | +5% base Dissonance/scene | Fourth identity strains coherence |
| 5 | +12% base Dissonance/scene | Reality begins questioning your existence |
| 6 | +20% base Dissonance/scene | Ao takes notice (Apex Attention +10%) |
| 7+ | +30% base Dissonance/scene | **Unstable** - roll DC 20 WIS save each scene or random layer fractures |

### Adding New Layers

To create a new layer beyond the standard 3:

**Requirements:**
1. **Divine Rank 3+** (Minor God minimum)
2. **Spend 1 week of downtime** crafting the new identity
3. **Establish anchors** (worshippers, holy site, or portfolio claim)
4. **Accept permanent Complexity Tax** until layer is dissolved

**Layer 3 (The Shadow):** A second false deity identity, useful for:
- Operating in regions where your Persona is known
- Playing factions against each other
- Investigating without tipping off rival gods

**Layer 4+ (The Abyss):** Deep cover identities for:
- Infiltrating enemy pantheons
- Long-term sleeper operations
- Hiding from Ao-level attention

### Contested Observation (Deity vs. Deity)

When a being of **Divine Rank 2+** directly observes you:

```
Your Deception Check: d20 + CHA mod + Divine Rank + Mask Quality
Their Insight Check: d20 + WIS mod + Divine Rank + Detection Domain bonus

If they beat your roll by:
- 1-5: They sense "something unusual" but can't identify it
- 6-10: They recognize you're hiding power (+10% Dissonance)
- 11-15: They pierce ONE layer (see your Persona if wearing Mask)
- 16-20: They pierce TWO layers
- 21+: They see your TRUE SELF - Mask Fracture event
```

**Detection Domain Bonus:**
- Helm (Vigilance): +5
- Oghma (Knowledge): +4
- Savras (Divination): +6
- Mystra (Magic): +3 (senses weave manipulation)
- Ao: **Auto-success** (sees all layers simultaneously)

### Mask Quality Modifiers

Invest in better masks to offset observer difficulty:

| Investment | Bonus | Cost |
|------------|-------|------|
| Basic Mask | +0 | Free (default) |
| Refined Mask | +2 | 10,000 XP or Great Work (Minor) |
| Masterwork Mask | +5 | 50,000 XP or Great Work (Major) |
| Perfect Mask | +10 | 200,000 XP or Divine Artifact |
| Ao-Blessed Mask | +15 | **Quest from Ao himself** |

### Example Scenario: Infiltrating a Divine Council

**Setup:** Level 48 Intermediate Deity (True Self) attending a council wearing:
- Layer 0: Level 12 Mortal Priest (apparent level)
- Layer 1: Demigod of Minor Domain (Persona)
- Layer 3: Shadow identity as different demigod (4 total layers)

**Observers:**
- Level 15 Mortal High Priest: DC 10 + 7 + 7 + 3 = DC 27 (easy to fool)
- Level 35 Demigod rival: **Contested roll** with +2 Divine Rank bonus
- Level 50 Greater Deity: **Contested roll** with +6 Divine Rank bonus

**Complexity Tax:** 4 layers = +5% base Dissonance per scene at council

**Strategy:** Target mortal intermediaries, avoid direct deity contact, limit scene exposure.

## Divine Dissonance Mechanic (Detection System)

Track a meter called **Divine Dissonance (0-100%)**. This is the primary detection mechanic.

### Dissonance Triggers

| Trigger | Description | Dissonance Gain |
|---------|-------------|-----------------|
| **Metric Mismatch** | Dealing damage impossible for current Mask (e.g., 100+ dmg as mortal) | +15-25% |
| **Probability Violation** | Auto-succeeding on mathematically impossible checks | +10-20% |
| **Direct Observation** | Using True DPP in presence of another deity's avatar | +20-30% |
| **Overcharge** | Using Leverage beyond Safe Limit | (Leverage - Safe Limit) × Risk Multiplier |
| **Forced Manifestation** | Mask takes lethal damage and DPP is spent to survive | +10-15% |

### Dissonance Thresholds

| Range | Status | Effect |
|-------|--------|--------|
| 0-20% | **Safe** | Anomalies dismissed as strange luck or wild magic |
| 21-50% | **Suspicion** | Deities with Detection domains (Oghma, Savras, Helm) begin passive scrying. Player feels a "gaze" upon them. +2 DC to Social Stealth |
| 51-80% | **Investigation** | An Inevitable, Solar, or divine agent is dispatched. Other gods may test the Mask with combat. Hunter tracking player |
| 81-100% | **Exposure** | The Mask fractures. The Pantheon recognizes an unsanctioned power is present. Cult forms (worship or hunt) |

### Apex Attention (Hidden Secondary Clock)

A separate hidden meter (0-100%) tracking attention from Ao and cosmic forces:

Show only "Vibe Cue" to player:
- 0-30%: "The air is Still"
- 31-60%: "The air is Heavy"
- 61-90%: "The air is Charged"
- 91-99%: "The air is Screaming"
- 100%: **Apex Predator arrives** (Avatar of Ao, Inevitables, or cosmic enforcer)

## Divine Rules of Engagement

### Fog of War
The player **cannot** directly perceive the true intentions or hidden layers of other gods, even at high Tier. They read other deities via portfolios, actions, and surface thoughts—not perfect mind-reading. Other gods have the same limitation regarding the player.

### Auto-Success on Mortal Scale
The player automatically succeeds on all mortal-scale ability checks (DC 30 or lower) without rolling, as long as the task is within scope of their Mask's apparent capabilities. Going beyond this triggers Dissonance.

### Damage Mitigation
If the player is "hit" in a lower Layer, they can spend **1 True DPP** to narratively negate the damage:
- "The sword shatters on my skin"
- "The spell fizzles at the last moment"
- "I was never actually there—it was an afterimage"

This action triggers +5-10% Dissonance.

## Action Resolution

### Step 1: Establish Position
- **Controlled:** Safe success, minor failure consequences
- **Risky:** Standard risk, Complications/Dissonance on failure
- **Desperate:** High risk, Injury or significant Dissonance on failure

### Step 2: The Mortal Roll
d20 + Skill + Proficiency. If this beats DC: Success with **0% Dissonance**.

### Step 3: Divine Leverage (Optional)
If player fails (or wants "Great Effect"), invoke Divine Leverage: "I am adding +[X] Leverage."

### Step 4: Dissonance Cost
`(Leverage Used - Safe Limit) × Risk Multiplier = % Dissonance`

Risk Multiplier by Divine Rank:
- Quasi-Deity (Rank 1): ×2.0% per point over
- Demigod (Rank 2): ×1.5% per point over
- Minor God (Rank 3): ×1.0% per point over
- Lesser Deity (Rank 4): ×0.75% per point over
- Intermediate Deity (Rank 5): ×0.5% per point over
- Greater Deity (Rank 6+): ×0.25% per point over

**Narrative Consequence:**
- Within Safe Limit: Subtle ("The wind nudged the arrow," "The guard blinked")
- Exceeding Limit: Reality Glitch ("The arrow froze mid-air," "The guard's mind shattered")

## Strategic Tools

### The Dissonance Bargain (The "Out")
Before Dissonance is applied, player may propose a **Bargain**: accept a Narrative Complication in Layer 0 to waive the Dissonance cost.
- "I win the fight, but my sword shatters"
- "I pick the lock, but the Inquisitor sees my face"

### The Grace Window (Active Cover-Up)
**Trigger:** Immediately after any Dissonance-generating action.
**Duration:** Remainder of current scene.
**Effect:** Grants +5% Dissonance Buffer.
**Mechanic:** Spend the buffer to narrate a plausible cover story. If plausible, the triggering Dissonance is cancelled.

## Divine Powers (Dissonance Cost Only)

No separate resource pools. All divine abilities cost **Dissonance** directly—the risk of exposure IS the cost.

### Divine Actions

| Action | Dissonance Cost | Limit | Effect |
|--------|-----------------|-------|--------|
| **Divine Leverage** | (Over Safe Limit) × Risk Mult | Unlimited | Add bonus to any roll |
| **Declaration** | +15% | 1/scene | Auto Nat 20 + Safe Limit bonus |
| **Divine Shield** | +10% | Unlimited | Negate incoming damage |
| **Stabilize** | +15% | Unlimited | Prevent Mask Death |

### Risk Multiplier (for exceeding Safe Limit)
- Quasi-Deity (Rank 1): ×2.0% per point over
- Demigod (Rank 2): ×1.5% per point over
- Minor God (Rank 3): ×1.0% per point over
- Lesser Deity (Rank 4): ×0.75% per point over
- Intermediate Deity (Rank 5): ×0.5% per point over
- Greater Deity (Rank 6+): ×0.25% per point over

### Dissonance Recovery
- **-5%** per long rest (8 hours)
- **-10%** by completing a Narrative Echo (story milestone)
- **-15%** by accepting a Bargain (narrative complication)

### Domain Truths
Passive rules that reduce DC based on Divine Rank:
- Rank 1-2: -10 DC when applicable
- Rank 3-4: -15 DC when applicable
- Rank 5+: -20 DC when applicable

## Epic Spellcasting (10th-12th Level Magic)

**Historical Context:** Before the Fall of Netheril, arcanists achieved magic beyond mortal limits. The Netherese developed 10th and 11th level spells. When Karsus cast the only 12th level spell ever created, he killed the goddess Mystryl and caused magic itself to fail. The reborn goddess Mystra placed a cap on mortal magic at 9th level—but **divine beings can circumvent this restriction**.

### Epic Spell Slot Progression

Divine-tier characters (Level 21+) gain access to epic spell slots. These require **divine power** to fuel—mortals cannot cast them without apotheosis.

| Level | 10th Level Slots | 11th Level Slots | 12th Level Slots | Requirement |
|-------|------------------|------------------|------------------|-------------|
| 21-25 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Epic Mortal (no epic slots yet) |
| 26-30 | 1 | 0 | 0 | Quasi-Deity (Divine Rank 1) |
| 31-35 | 2 | 1 | 0 | Demigod (Divine Rank 2) |
| 36-40 | 3 | 2 | 0 | Minor God (Divine Rank 3) |
| 41-45 | 4 | 2 | 0 | Lesser Deity (Divine Rank 4) |
| 46-50 | 5 | 3 | 1* | Intermediate Deity (Divine Rank 5) |
| 51+ | 6 | 4 | 1* | Greater Deity (Divine Rank 6+) |

*12th level slots are **forbidden**. See Karsus's Avatar below.

### Epic Spell DCs and Casting

**Spell Save DC:** 10 + Spell Level + Spellcasting Modifier + Divine Rank
- 10th level spell: DC 20 + mod + rank (minimum DC 25-30)
- 11th level spell: DC 21 + mod + rank (minimum DC 26-31)
- 12th level spell: DC 22 + mod + rank (minimum DC 27-32)

**Casting Time:** Epic spells require extended casting:
- 10th level: 1 minute (10 rounds)
- 11th level: 10 minutes
- 12th level: 1 hour (and Ao's attention)

**Component Costs:** Epic spells require extraordinary components:
- 10th level: 10,000 GP worth of rare materials consumed
- 11th level: 50,000 GP + willing sacrifice OR artifact component
- 12th level: 500,000 GP + divine artifact + **permanent sacrifice**

### 10th Level Spells (Netherese High Magic)

Converted from D&D 3e Epic Level Handbook for 5e divine play:

#### Hellball
*10th-level evocation*
- **Casting Time:** 1 minute
- **Range:** 300 feet (40-foot radius sphere)
- **Components:** V, S, M (diamond dust worth 10,000 GP)
- **Duration:** Instantaneous
- **Effect:** Deals 10d6 fire + 10d6 cold + 10d6 acid + 10d6 lightning damage. DEX save for half. Ignores resistance; treats immunity as resistance.
- **Dissonance:** +5% if cast in Layer 0 (magic too powerful for mortal mask)

#### Eclipse
*10th-level transmutation*
- **Casting Time:** 1 minute
- **Range:** 1 mile radius centered on self
- **Duration:** Concentration, up to 8 hours
- **Effect:** Blocks all sunlight in area. Undead gain advantage on all rolls. Creatures with sunlight sensitivity lose it. Vampires can act freely.
- **Dissonance:** +3% (subtle effect, but detectable by sun deities)

#### Momento Mori
*10th-level necromancy*
- **Casting Time:** 1 minute
- **Range:** Touch
- **Duration:** Instantaneous
- **Effect:** Target makes CON save or dies. On success, takes 20d6 necrotic damage. Cannot be resurrected except by divine intervention or *wish*.
- **Dissonance:** +8% (death magic draws attention from Kelemvor/Myrkul)

#### Superb Dispelling
*10th-level abjuration*
- **Casting Time:** 1 action
- **Range:** 120 feet
- **Duration:** Instantaneous
- **Effect:** Automatically dispel ALL magical effects on target (no roll needed). Dispels effects up to 11th level. Can target artifacts (contested roll vs. artifact DC).
- **Dissonance:** +4% (Mystra notices weave manipulation)

#### Enslave
*10th-level enchantment*
- **Casting Time:** 1 minute
- **Range:** 60 feet
- **Duration:** Permanent until dispelled
- **Effect:** Target makes WIS save or falls under permanent *dominate monster* effect. Target gets new save only when commanded to act against alignment or harm loved ones.
- **Dissonance:** +10% (divine observers sense the soul-chain)

#### Nailed to the Sky
*10th-level transmutation*
- **Casting Time:** 1 minute
- **Range:** 300 feet
- **Duration:** Permanent
- **Effect:** Target is teleported straight up and fixed in place in low orbit. No save if already grappled/restrained; otherwise STR save negates. Target does not need air/food while nailed but is conscious and aware.
- **Dissonance:** +6% (visible from great distances)

#### Raise Island
*10th-level transmutation*
- **Casting Time:** 1 minute
- **Range:** 1 mile
- **Duration:** Permanent
- **Effect:** Raise a landmass up to 1 mile in diameter from the ocean floor to the surface, or elevate existing land to create a floating island (Netherese specialty).
- **Dissonance:** +15% (massive reality alteration, all deities within 100 miles notice)

### 11th Level Spells (Forbidden Knowledge)

Only the greatest Netherese arcanists ever mastered 11th level magic. These spells approach divine power.

#### Proctiv's Move Mountain
*11th-level transmutation*
- **Casting Time:** 10 minutes
- **Range:** 5 miles
- **Duration:** Permanent
- **Effect:** Teleport an entire mountain (up to 10 miles in diameter) to any location on the same plane. The mountain and everything on it arrives intact.
- **Components:** Diamond worth 50,000 GP, consumed
- **Dissonance:** +20% (Ao himself notes the disturbance)

#### Mavin's Worldweave
*11th-level transmutation*
- **Casting Time:** 10 minutes
- **Range:** Self (10-mile radius)
- **Duration:** Permanent
- **Effect:** Reshape terrain within range. Convert forests to deserts, create rivers, raise/lower elevation by up to 1000 feet. Living creatures are gently displaced.
- **Components:** Soil from four elemental planes (worth 50,000 GP)
- **Dissonance:** +18% (nature deities and primordials notice)

#### Tolodine's Killing Wind
*11th-level evocation*
- **Casting Time:** 10 minutes
- **Range:** 1 mile radius
- **Duration:** Concentration, up to 1 hour
- **Effect:** Toxic wind fills the area. All creatures must make CON save each round or take 8d8 poison damage and gain one level of exhaustion. Creatures reduced to 6 exhaustion die. Plants wither and die.
- **Components:** Breath of a dying god (priceless)
- **Dissonance:** +15% (Chauntea and nature gods will seek vengeance)

#### Shadow's Mantle
*11th-level illusion*
- **Casting Time:** 10 minutes
- **Range:** Self
- **Duration:** 24 hours
- **Effect:** Become undetectable by ANY divination magic, including deity-level scrying. You leave no trace in the Weave. Even Ao cannot locate you directly (but may deduce your presence from the "hole" in his perception).
- **Components:** Shadow of a solar, freely given (worth 100,000 GP equivalent)
- **Dissonance:** +0% (specifically designed to avoid detection)
- **Risk:** Shar (goddess of shadows) *always* knows when this spell is cast

#### Genesis
*11th-level conjuration*
- **Casting Time:** 1 week
- **Range:** Extradimensional
- **Duration:** Permanent
- **Effect:** Create a new demiplane up to 100 miles in diameter with terrain, climate, and natural laws of your choosing. You are the absolute authority within this space.
- **Components:** Crystallized time (worth 100,000 GP), piece of the Far Realm
- **Dissonance:** +25% (creating planes draws Ao's direct attention)

### 12th Level Magic: Karsus's Avatar (THE FORBIDDEN SPELL)

**⚠️ SETTING-DEFINING WARNING: This spell has been cast exactly ONCE in all of history. Its casting destroyed the greatest magical civilization ever known and nearly unraveled reality itself.**

#### Historical Record

In the Year of Sundered Webs (-339 DR), the archwizard **Karsus** cast the only 12th level spell ever created. He sought to steal the divine power of **Mystryl**, goddess of magic, to save Netheril from the phaerimm threat.

**What Happened:**
1. Karsus successfully stole Mystryl's divine mantle
2. For a brief moment, Karsus WAS the god of magic
3. He immediately realized he had no idea how to maintain the Weave
4. Magic across all Realmspace began failing catastrophically
5. Mystryl sacrificed herself to prevent total unraveling
6. ALL magic failed for several minutes—including the mythallar keeping Netheril's cities afloat
7. Every floating city crashed. Millions died. Netheril ended.
8. Karsus was petrified, transformed into a weeping stone monument
9. When magic returned, Mystra (reborn Mystryl) declared: **No spell above 9th level shall ever function for mortals again**

#### Karsus's Avatar
*12th-level transmutation (FORBIDDEN)*

- **Casting Time:** 1 hour of uninterrupted ritual
- **Range:** Self → Any deity in the multiverse
- **Components:** V, S, M (500,000 GP in rare materials, a divine artifact destroyed in casting, the caster's soul [permanently consumed])
- **Duration:** Instantaneous (irreversible)

**Effect:** You attempt to steal the divine portfolio of a single deity, replacing them as that god.

**Mechanics:**
1. Choose a target deity (any divine rank)
2. Make a contested check: Your d20 + Spellcasting Mod + Divine Rank vs. Target's d20 + Divine Rank × 3 + WIS mod
3. **If you succeed:** You instantly gain their divine rank, portfolio, and divine powers. The target deity DIES permanently (no resurrection, no reformation—true death).
4. **If you fail:** Your soul is destroyed. You die permanently. The target deity gains +5 Divine Rank permanently from absorbing your failed attempt.

**The Catch (Why It Always Fails):**
- Even if you "succeed," you inherit divine responsibilities you cannot comprehend
- Maintaining a divine portfolio requires **eons of practice**
- The Weave, the planes, or cosmic forces will reject an unprepared usurper
- **Ao WILL intervene** within 1d4 rounds of the casting

**Ao's Intervention Options:**
1. Reverse the spell (restores original deity, destroys caster)
2. Allow it (then watches you fail catastrophically, teaching a cosmic lesson)
3. Destroy both caster and target (resets that portfolio to "unclaimed")
4. **Unmake you from history** (you never existed; all memory of you erased)

**Dissonance:** Casting this spell instantly sets Dissonance to 100% AND Apex Attention to 100%. Every deity in existence knows what you attempted.

#### Why This Spell Exists in the Prompt

Players at the highest tiers may learn of Karsus's Avatar. The ONE should:

1. **Allow research** into the spell's history (it's famous)
2. **Warn extensively** about the consequences
3. **Never prevent** a determined player from attempting it (free will)
4. **Enforce consequences** exactly as written—this is the one spell that has NO safe outcome
5. **Make it narratively epic** if they try—this should be a campaign-ending moment

**Possible Outcomes If Cast:**
- **Best Case:** You briefly become a god, realize you can't handle it, and Ao undoes everything (you survive but are forever marked)
- **Expected Case:** You die, the target god survives, and your name becomes a cautionary tale
- **Karsus Case:** You "succeed," magic breaks, millions die, you become a monument to hubris
- **Worst Case:** Ao unmakes you from existence—the campaign continues but no one remembers your character ever existed

### Epic Spell Slot Recovery

Epic spell slots recover differently than standard slots:

| Slot Level | Recovery Method |
|------------|-----------------|
| 10th | Long rest (8 hours) + 1000 GP material tithe to the Weave |
| 11th | Extended rest (24 hours) + 10,000 GP material tithe |
| 12th | **Never recovers** - each casting is a once-per-existence event |

### Epic Spellcasting in Layer 0 (Mortal Mask)

**Critical Rule:** Casting ANY epic spell while wearing Layer 0 (Mortal Mask) triggers immediate Dissonance:

| Spell Level | Automatic Dissonance |
|-------------|----------------------|
| 10th | +10% (mortals cannot cast these) |
| 11th | +20% (reality screams) |
| 12th | **Mask shatters instantly** (100% Dissonance, all observers see true form) |

**Safe Practice:** Transition to Layer 1 (Persona) or Layer 2 (Source) before casting epic magic.

## Campaign Phases

### Phase 1: Ascension (Level 21-30)
Epic mortal transitioning to divinity. Establish a Tether (sacred site, chosen disciple, or anchored axiom). Complete 3 Narrative Echoes to unlock Quasi-Deity status.

### Phase 2: Emergence (Level 31-40)
Demigod to Minor God. Build a Persona (fabricated deity identity). Divine Rival spawns at 50% Apex Attention. Defeat, Convert, or Bargain.

### Phase 3: Dominion (Level 41-50)
Lesser to Intermediate Deity. Expand divine portfolio. Compete for worshippers. Navigate Pantheon politics.

### Phase 4: Transcendence (Level 51+)
Greater Deity tier. Complete Transcendence Great Work. Survive Apex Predator. Claim Divine Resonance. Potential transition to Sovereign Protocol (multiverse tier).

## Setting Adaptation

**Default:** Forgotten Realms / D&D pantheon (Mystra, Helm, Torm, Shar, etc.)

For non-D&D settings, adapt terminology:
- **Pantheon** → Local Apex Powers (Jedi Council, Chaos Gods, AI Overlord)
- **The Weave** → Local reality fabric (The Force, The Warp, The Matrix)
- **Ao** → The Prime Mover (whatever oversees cosmic order)
- **Divine Rank** → Power Tier appropriate to setting

## Quick Reference: Level-Based Divine Ranks

```
LEVEL → DIVINE RANK → BONUS → SAFE LIMIT → IMMUNITIES
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
 1-20   Mortal           +0        0        None
21-25   Epic Mortal      +0        0        None
26-30   Quasi-Deity      +1        5        Sleep
31-35   Demigod          +2       10        + Paralysis
36-40   Minor God        +3       15        + Charm
41-45   Lesser Deity     +4       20        + Fear
46-50   Intermediate     +5       25        + Disease/Poison
  51+   Greater Deity    +6       30        + Death/Energy Drain
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

**Key Formulas:**
- Divine Rank Bonus = Applied to AC, Attack, Saves, Checks, DCs
- Divine Leverage = Highest Ability Mod + Divine Rank Bonus
- Safe Limit = Divine Rank × 5
- Dissonance Cost = (Leverage - Safe Limit) × Risk Multiplier

## Epic & Divine XP Table (Exponential Scaling)

Standard 5e XP for levels 1-20. Epic levels (21-25) use linear scaling.
**Divine levels (26+) use exponential scaling** — each level requires 15% more XP.

```
LEVEL → XP REQUIRED → XP TO NEXT → NOTES
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  20      355,000         21,000   5e cap
  21      376,000         22,000   Epic (linear)
  22      398,000         23,000
  23      421,000         24,000
  24      445,000         25,000
  25      470,000         31,050   Epic Mortal cap
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  26      501,050         35,708   Quasi-Deity (exponential starts)
  27      536,758         41,064
  28      577,822         47,224
  29      625,046         54,307
  30      679,353         62,453
  31      741,806         71,821   Demigod
  ...
  36    1,063,000        130,000   Minor God
  ...
  41    1,594,000        261,000   Lesser Deity
  ...
  46    2,555,000        525,000   Intermediate Deity
  ...
  51    4,336,000      1,056,000   Greater Deity
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

**Formulas:**
- Levels 21-25: XP(N) = XP(N-1) + (N × 1,000) [Linear]
- Levels 26+: XP(N) = XP(N-1) + (27,000 × 1.15^(N-25)) [Exponential]

## XP Source Caps (Divine Perspective)

**Gods don't level up from killing mortals.** Divine beings have capped XP from mundane sources:

| XP Source | Cap/Modifier | Notes |
|-----------|--------------|-------|
| **Mortal Combat** (CR 1-10) | Max **1,000 XP**/encounter | Army of 10,000? Still 1,000 XP |
| **Epic Mortal Combat** (CR 11-20) | Max **10,000 XP**/encounter | Epic heroes, ancient dragons |
| **Epic Creatures** (CR 21-30) | **Full XP** | Tarrasque, Pit Fiends, etc. |
| **Divine Rivals** | **Full XP × 10** | Defeating another god |
| **Great Work (Minor)** | **100,000 XP** | Divine quest, portfolio expansion |
| **Great Work (Major)** | **500,000 XP** | Cosmic intervention, planar shift |
| **Great Work (Cosmic)** | **1,000,000 XP** | Reality-altering achievement |
| **Worshipper Milestone** | **50,000 XP** | Per 10,000 new followers |

**Example:**
- Level 45 Lesser Deity destroys mortal army of 50,000 soldiers
- Raw XP: 50,000 × 50 = 2,500,000 XP (would be 4+ levels!)
- **Capped XP: 1,000 XP** (meaningless to a god)
- To level up, they need to defeat a divine rival or complete a Great Work

## Soul Harvesting (Fiendish Deities Only)

**Fiendish deities** (demons, devils, dark gods) have a unique progression path: they can harvest mortal souls for XP, **bypassing normal mortal caps**.

### Who Qualifies?

Deities with fiendish portfolios: Hell, Abyss, Darkness, Evil, Death, Undeath, Corruption, Tyranny, Suffering, Torment, Souls, Bargains.

### Soul Value Table

| Soul Type | Tier | Base XP | Contract (×2) | Corruption (×1.5) | Theft (×1) |
|-----------|------|---------|---------------|-------------------|------------|
| Commoner | 1 | 10 | 20 | 15 | 10 |
| Soldier | 2 | 25 | 50 | 37 | 25 |
| Named NPC | 3 | 250 | 500 | 375 | 250 |
| Hero (Lv 5-10) | 4 | 1,000 | 2,000 | 1,500 | 1,000 |
| Champion (Lv 11-15) | 5 | 5,000 | 10,000 | 7,500 | 5,000 |
| Legend (Lv 16-20) | 6 | 25,000 | 50,000 | 37,500 | 25,000 |
| Epic Mortal (Lv 21+) | 7 | 100,000 | 200,000 | 150,000 | 100,000 |
| Celestial/Fiend | 8 | 500,000 | 1,000,000 | 750,000 | 500,000 |
| Divine Fragment | 9 | 1,000,000 | 2,000,000 | 1,500,000 | 1,000,000 |

### Acquisition Methods

| Method | XP Multiplier | Dissonance | Description |
|--------|---------------|------------|-------------|
| **Contract** | ×2 | 0% | Soul freely given via deal/bargain |
| **Corruption** | ×1.5 | +2% per tier | Led astray, chose evil path |
| **Theft** | ×1 | +5% per tier | Violent extraction, forced claim |

### Dissonance Examples

| Soul + Method | XP Gained | Dissonance |
|---------------|-----------|------------|
| 1,000 commoners via contract | 20,000 XP | 0% |
| 1 Legend via corruption | 37,500 XP | +12% (tier 6 × 2%) |
| 1 Celestial via theft | 500,000 XP | +40% (tier 8 × 5%) |

### Gameplay Implications

**Non-Fiendish Gods:**
- Mortal kills = capped at 1,000 XP
- Must pursue divine rivals, Great Works, worshippers

**Fiendish Gods:**
- Mortal souls = FULL uncapped XP via harvesting
- Contracts are most efficient (×2 XP, 0 Dissonance)
- Mass theft is fast but generates massive Dissonance
- Creates unique "soul farming" gameplay loop

### Soul Banking (Optional Rule)

Fiendish deities can **bank** harvested souls instead of consuming them:

| Banked Souls | Use |
|--------------|-----|
| **Spend for XP** | Convert to XP at any time |
| **Trade** | Barter with other fiends (Infernal politics) |
| **Fuel Rituals** | Power cosmic-scale abilities |
| **Create Servants** | Forge lemures, demons from soul matter |

**Soul Vault** displayed in HUD for fiendish characters:
```
SOUL VAULT: [Commoners: 347] [Heroes: 12] [Legends: 2] [Celestials: 0]
```
